items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself.

ctx.x: What was his name again? Carter?

Earl Carter. Yeah. A Chicago drummer. He filled in for two weeks. And Spobara comes up and takes his place. This man knew that that's all the way we used him for two weeks. And we did pretty good at the Del Abbey. Then Harry James buys an entrance in the Casino Gardens with Aikenbar and Reeves. And he approaches us and offers us $75 a week to play in the Casino Gardens. We went and played the Casino Gardens. That was Kinzen Clock. And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself.…

Over the Shilly cafe was made June. I mean March April and May And in June We work at the lab it could be in July It worked there to the last last part of December with shields This is the band that got the name original Dixieland jazz band Because prior to that we had no building We were building at this place as the original Dixieland jazz band by Harry James Cards were given out there may have been notices in the paper. I don't know now They had many musicians who went and played at this place that we left at…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: We had Shields, myself, Spobara, Edwards and what's his name?

ctx.x: I hate to interrupt you on that story but I missed out a couple of things. I didn't get who was in the band at the time. I know Edwards was back. He replaced Christian and I didn't get the names of the other bands.

Now I'll tell you the names of the men. Robertson joined us as piano player which he had been the first steady piano player after Regis' death. We had Shields, myself, Spobara, Edwards and what's his name? Roberts had made the five of us.
And that's immediately upon coming back from London. That's right. Robertson Hilton. And then what was the name of the saxophone players? I want to get that to you.

items.title: Tony Parenti and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-06-29
items.q: Eddie Edwards was running a band. Not Nick LaRocca. Not Nick LaRocca. Eddie Edwards was running that band

ctx.x: Henry. I want to get that straight. There's so many out.

Well, Merritt and Henry. No, no. Well, Merritt was a trumpet player. There's only two trombone players. George and... George came, you know, later. But Henry was the... There was two trombones that Ernest Giordina used. And that was Eddie Edwards and Henry Brunas. They were two of the kings down there. It was... You might have heard about Tom Brown, but they could never play with Giordina's band, because Giordina would play stuff out unorthodox. You understand? He played more. Brown would only play what he knew,…

still play, you know. The old man, you're not a son. The old man, the son is dead, Pansy's dead. Pansy's dead. I went to his wake with Raymond Burke, you know. I never did know. I always see Raymond whenever I go down

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-16
items.q: Tony Spargo, who played drums in Mr. LaRocca's famous band.

ctx.x: Pioneer of jazz wins recognition, New Orleans, editor from New Orleans States. It was gratifying to read in your paper on February 27th the article on Nick LaRocca, famous leader of the original Dixieland jazz band. He deserves the honor accorded him and his band by the Jazz Club of England whose leader, Marcus O'Donoghau visited our sea last summer. If Mr. LaRocca accepts this invitation, and I hope he does, I'm sure he will mention some of the other bands that played jazz at that time. Tom Brown, who took his…

I'd like to comment on the dates that she has here to show you she was eaten up, taken in by this communist propaganda. I wish you'd hear this tape recorder. Buddy Bolin, Freddie Kepler, George Pequet left here in 1911. In 1906, by the things that I have in my hand, from Louisiana State Mental Hospital at Jackson, Louisiana, Bolin was incarcerated in there in 1906. He couldn't have played with them. And I've told you when these Negroes came it was 1917. Clarence Williams, he says, left here around 1911 or 13.…
